userStories.notes: Planning story completed. Generated 11 stories (US-49-002 through US-49-012) addressing the 6 user-reported download_segments issues: P0 cookie propagation for Python API, P0 ImpersonateTarget type fix, P1 stall detection wrapper for ydl.download(), P2 global escalation state with bot-detection abort, P2 DNS/network failure pattern matching for Python API, plus hardening stories for circuit breaker wiring, download_segments subprocess migration path, error reporting improvements, and test coverage. Sprint-48 laid the infrastructure (socket timeout, escalation integration, metrics, checkpoint validation); sprint-49 fixes the remaining functional bugs that prevent download_segments from actually working.

userStories.title: Add cookie propagation to download_segments Python API calls
acceptanceCriteria: Add 'cookiesfrombrowser' key to ydl_opts dict in _download_segments() reading from download config (e.g., ['firefox'])
Add fallback to 'cookiefile' path in ydl_opts if cookiesfrombrowser is not configured or fails
Add 'cookies_from_browser' field to DownloadConfig dataclass in src/config/sections/download.py with default None
Add 'cookies_from_browser' entry to config.yaml download section with comment explaining Python API vs CLI behavior
Add unit test verifying cookiesfrombrowser is injected into ydl_opts when configured
Add unit test verifying cookiefile fallback is used when cookies_from_browser is not set but cookie_rotation provides a cookie path
userStories.notes: P0 fix - Issue #4 from user interview. Tier: bug fix. The yt-dlp Python API does not read ~/.config/yt-dlp/config, so download_segments.py gets zero cookies while the CLI subprocess in core.py inherits --cookies-from-browser firefox. Without cookies, every Python API request triggers 'Sign in to confirm you're not a bot.' Source files: src/stages/download_segments.py:448-460 (ydl_opts construction), src/config/sections/download.py (add cookies_from_browser field), config.yaml (download section). The yt-dlp Python API key is 'cookiesfrombrowser' (list, e.g. ['firefox']) — different from CLI --cookies-from-browser. Also support 'cookiefile' as fallback from cookie_rotation config.

userStories.title: Fix ImpersonateTarget type conversion in _apply_escalation_to_ydl_opts
acceptanceCriteria: Replace raw string assignment ydl_opts['impersonate'] = value with ImpersonateTarget.from_str() conversion in _apply_escalation_to_ydl_opts()
Lowercase the client and os fields after parsing (e.g., 'Chrome-136' -> 'chrome-136', 'Macos-15' -> 'macos-15')
Add try/except guard around ImpersonateTarget conversion that falls back to no impersonation on failure rather than crashing with AssertionError
Add unit test verifying ImpersonateTarget object (not string) is set in ydl_opts after escalation translation
Add unit test verifying case-insensitive matching works (uppercase input produces lowercase target fields)
userStories.notes: Fixed _apply_escalation_to_ydl_opts to convert raw impersonate string to ImpersonateTarget object with lowercased client/os fields. Added try/except fallback. Updated 4 existing tests + added 3 new tests (object type, lowercase fields, invalid input fallback). 79/79 tests pass.

userStories.title: Add process-level stall detection wrapper around ydl.download() call
acceptanceCriteria: Wrap the ydl.download() call in a concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor with configurable timeout (default from stall_timeout config, fallback 120s)
On timeout, log a warning with video_id and elapsed time, then raise a TimeoutError that feeds into the existing retry/escalation logic
Add 'segment_stall_timeout' field to DownloadConfig dataclass with default matching existing stall_timeout (60s) or a higher value suitable for segments
Add unit test verifying that a simulated stall (mocked ydl.download that sleeps) triggers timeout and raises
Add unit test verifying successful downloads within timeout are not interrupted
userStories.notes: Implemented process-level stall detection using concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor around ydl.download(). Added segment_stall_timeout=120 to DownloadConfig and config.yaml. When timeout=0, falls back to unwrapped call. On stall, logs warning with video_id/elapsed and raises TimeoutError that feeds into existing retry/escalation. Added 4 tests: stall triggers timeout, success not interrupted, disabled when 0, reads from config. Also added defensive int() conversion for MagicMock compatibility with existing tests. 83/83 tests pass.

userStories.title: Add global bot-detection counter with escalation tier floor
acceptanceCriteria: Add a stage-level consecutive_bot_detection counter that increments on any 403/bot-detection error across all video IDs
When counter exceeds configurable threshold (default 5), set a global tier floor so subsequent downloads start at max escalation tier instead of Tier 1
Stop resetting the network failure abort counter on bot-detection errors — treat widespread bot-detection as a stage-level failure signal
Reset bot-detection counter on any successful download
Add unit test verifying tier floor propagation after N consecutive bot-detection errors across different video IDs
Add unit test verifying bot-detection errors no longer reset the network failure counter
userStories.notes: P2 fix - Issue #6 from user interview. Tier: resilience improvement. Each video_id currently creates fresh escalation state starting at Tier 1 (download_segments.py:464-466). When YouTube blocks broadly, every video independently fails at Tier 1 then gets queued for retry — wasting time on doomed requests. Bot-detection errors also reset the network failure abort counter (download_segments.py:558-560), preventing early abort. Need a stage-level signal that propagates the 'YouTube is blocking everything' state. The EscalationManager.set_circuit_breaker() exists but is never called — wire it up. Source files: src/stages/download_segments.py:464-466, 536-560, src/downloader/escalation_manager.py:330 (circuit breaker shortcut logic).

userStories.title: Validate and extend _is_network_failure() patterns for Python API error format
acceptanceCriteria: Audit _is_network_failure() regex patterns against actual Python API DownloadError message format (which wraps exceptions differently than subprocess stderr)
Add pattern for Windows DNS failure 'Errno 11001' and ffmpeg exit code '4294967158' (0xFFFFFEC6) if not already covered
Add pattern for 'URLError' and 'ConnectionResetError' which are common Python API network error wrappers
Add unit test with 6+ real-world error message strings from both Python API and subprocess stderr verifying correct classification
Add unit test verifying bot-detection messages ('Sign in to confirm', 'HTTP Error 403') are NOT classified as network failures
userStories.notes: P2 fix - Issue #3 from user interview. Tier: correctness improvement. _is_network_failure() at download_segments.py:29-63 pattern-matches against error messages, but Python API exceptions format differently than subprocess stderr. For example, yt_dlp.utils.DownloadError wraps the original exception with 'ERROR: ...' prefix. The function needs to handle both formats. Also verify that ffmpeg exit code 4294967158 (unsigned representation of -314 signed) is detected. Source files: src/stages/download_segments.py:29-63 (_is_network_failure function), lines 536-557 (abort logic).

userStories.title: Wire circuit breaker into download_segments escalation manager
acceptanceCriteria: Call escalation_manager.set_circuit_breaker(circuit_breaker) during download_segments stage initialization when both components are available
Verify the circuit breaker shortcut logic at escalation_manager.py:330 fires when circuit is open (skips to max tier)
Add circuit breaker state check before each download attempt — if circuit is open and no higher tiers available, skip the video and add to retry queue
Add unit test verifying set_circuit_breaker() is called during stage init
Add unit test verifying open circuit causes escalation to skip to max tier
userStories.notes: Tier: infrastructure wiring. The EscalationManager has set_circuit_breaker() and shortcut-to-max-tier logic at escalation_manager.py:330, but it's never called — self._circuit_breaker is always None. The circuit breaker (added in US-48-004) and escalation integration (US-48-005) exist independently but aren't connected. Wiring them together means the circuit breaker's failure tracking informs escalation decisions. Source files: src/stages/download_segments.py (stage init where escalation_manager and circuit_breaker are both available), src/downloader/escalation_manager.py:259-268 (set_circuit_breaker), lines 330-337 (shortcut logic).

userStories.title: Add bot-detection abort threshold to download_segments stage
acceptanceCriteria: Add a BOT_DETECTION_ABORT_THRESHOLD constant (default 10) — when total bot-detection errors exceed this across all videos, abort the stage with a clear message
Add configurable 'bot_detection_abort_threshold' to DownloadConfig with the default value
Log actionable guidance when aborting: suggest checking cookies, VPN, or waiting before retry
Checkpoint progress before aborting so --resume can pick up where it left off
Add unit test verifying stage aborts after threshold consecutive bot-detection errors
Add unit test verifying checkpoint is saved before abort
userStories.notes: Tier: resilience improvement. Currently bot-detection errors (403, 'Sign in') are classified as video-specific and reset the network failure counter (download_segments.py:558-560). This means the stage never aborts on widespread bot-detection — it keeps trying every remaining segment with doomed Tier 1 requests. With no cookies (Issue #4) or broken impersonation (Issue #5), this means the entire stage runs to completion hitting YouTube's block wall for every segment. Need a separate bot-detection counter that triggers stage abort. Source files: src/stages/download_segments.py:536-560 (abort logic section), src/config/sections/download.py.

userStories.title: Add download_segments error summary with actionable diagnostics
acceptanceCriteria: At stage completion, log a structured summary: total segments, succeeded, failed, cached, skipped with breakdown by error category
Include per-error-category counts (network, bot-detection, video-specific, timeout) in the summary
If >50% failures are bot-detection, log specific guidance: 'Most failures are bot-detection. Check cookie configuration.'
Add the error summary to stage metrics (StageMetrics) so it's available in checkpoint
Add unit test verifying error summary is generated with correct category counts
userStories.notes: Tier: observability improvement. The download_segments stage currently logs individual errors but has no end-of-stage summary that helps diagnose systemic issues. When cookies are missing (Issue #4), every error is bot-detection but the user sees N individual error logs without a clear signal. A structured summary with category breakdown and actionable guidance makes the root cause obvious. Source files: src/stages/download_segments.py:390-399 (existing metrics), lines 536-560 (error classification). Integrate with StageMetrics added in US-48-011.

userStories.title: Add retry queue escalation awareness with tier persistence across passes
acceptanceCriteria: When adding a video to the retry queue, include the last-used escalation tier so the retry starts at that tier or higher
In _process_retry_queue(), apply the stored tier floor when constructing ydl_opts for retried downloads
Add cookies and impersonation to retry queue ydl_opts using the same pattern as the primary download loop
Add unit test verifying retried downloads inherit the escalation tier from the original failure
Add unit test verifying cookies are present in retry queue ydl_opts
userStories.notes: Tier: resilience improvement. The retry queue in download_segments processes failed segments but constructs fresh ydl_opts without propagating the escalation tier that was in effect when the segment failed. A segment that failed at Tier 2 gets retried at Tier 1, wasting time on already-failed lower tiers. Also, if US-49-002 (cookies) fixes the primary loop but not the retry queue, retries still fail. Source files: src/stages/download_segments.py (retry queue section — _process_retry_queue and retry_queue data structure).

Add integration test verifying end-to-end flow: cookies injected, impersonation target is ImpersonateTarget object, socket_timeout present, escalation applied
Add integration test simulating 3 consecutive bot-detection errors followed by tier escalation and successful download
Add integration test simulating network failure abort after threshold consecutive DNS errors
Add integration test verifying checkpoint save includes downloaded segment paths
userStories.notes: Tier: test coverage. Sprint-48 added unit tests for individual features (socket timeout, escalation, metrics) but no integration test that verifies the full download_segments flow with all features working together. The 6 issues from the user interview are interconnected (cookies + impersonation + escalation + abort logic), so an integration test catches interaction bugs. Source files: tests/ (new test file test_download_segments_integration.py), src/stages/download_segments.py.

Persisting them to checkpoint.json enables post-run analysis, Ralph dashboard integration, and cross-sprint trend tracking. The checkpoint already has a save mechanism — extend it to include stage metrics. Source files: src/stages/download_segments.py:390-399 (StageMetrics), src/checkpoint.py (checkpoint save/restore).
